rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about those who transgressed may describe all three named peoples, or specifically Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون شاملا لجميع المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tughyān is extreme disobedience and injustice; each nation transgressed in its own land, with the plural distributive or contextually restricted to their lands.
rows.anchor: والطغيان شدة العصيان والظلم ومعنى طغيانهم في البلاد أن كل أمة من هؤلاء طغوا في بلدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tyrant's example emboldens subordinates to violate rights, while resentment fragments the community and weakens it against external enemies; thus tyranny multiplies corruption.
rows.anchor: فلا جرم كان الطغيان سببا لكثرة الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-bilād may refer to the lands already mentioned; the plural distributes the action so each nation transgressed in its own country.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التعريف في { البلاد } تعريف العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasād means a thing's bad condition and damage; its opposite is ṣalāḥ. Corruption brings divine anger, since God does not love corruption.
rows.anchor: سوء حال الشيء ولحاق الضر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pouring of punishment is a metaphor for its sudden arrival and comprehensive engulfment, like water poured on a bather or rain on land.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا مستعار لحلول العذاب دفعة وإحاطته بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor combines speed and abundance; it resembles the use of ifrāgh for pouring patience and the idiom of unleashing a raid.
rows.anchor: فوجه الشبه مركب من السرعة والكثرة ونظيره استعارة الإفراغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment came suddenly and decisively: ʿĀd mistook the wind-cloud for rain, Thamūd were seized by the cry, and Pharaoh's people were engulfed as the sea closed around them.
rows.anchor: وكان العذاب الذي أصاب هؤلاء عذابا مفاجئا قاضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sawṭ is a whip made from plaited leather, used to discipline horses and make them run faster.
rows.anchor: آلة ضرب تتخذ من جلود مضفورة تضرب بها الخيل للتأديب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Arabs use sawṭ al-ʿadhāb for any punishment that includes whipping; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the phrase here is not literal in that sense.
rows.anchor: وعن الفراء أن كلمة { سوط عذاب } يقولها العرب لكل عذاب يدخل فيه السوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive joins an adjective to its noun: God poured punishment like a whip, a vivid simile for swift impact.
rows.anchor: وإضافة { سوط } إلى { عذاب } من إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Lord is at the watch-post may be a concluding generalization that explains the punishment, or the answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: تذييل وتعليل لإصابتهم بسوط عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a conclusion, the watch-post statement reassures the Prophet that God supports His messengers and warns opponents that every tyrant and corrupter is watched.
rows.anchor: بأن الله ينصر رسله وتصريحا للمعاندين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it answers the oath, the phrase alludes to punishment of the polytheists: a watch-post guards against aggressors, while prior examples function as evidence before the result.
rows.anchor: تكون كناية عن تسليط العذاب على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord instead of using the first-person pronoun or the divine name hints that the Prophet's own Lord will punish his deniers in support of him.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن فاعل ذلك ربه الذي شأنه أن ينتصر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirsād can denote a place or time of watching; its instrumental sense is inapplicable here because raṣd means waiting and surveillance.
rows.anchor: فهو هنا إما للزمان أو المكان إذ الرصد الترقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic definite article makes God's watch universal: the image of sentries tracking an enemy stands for God's knowledge of every movement and His recompense of each deed.
rows.anchor: فهو تمثيل لعمومم علم الله تعالى بما يكون من أعمال العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The watch-post image implies that the punished peoples were not wronged; the preposition bi- marks location or circumstance.
rows.anchor: وفي ما يفيده من التعليل إيماء إلى أن الله لم يظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa and ammā make the next passage derive directly from the preceding general statement, although this inferential connection is initially obscure.
rows.anchor: دلت الفاء على أن الكلام الواقع بعدها متصل بما قبلها ومتفرع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples enjoyed blessings while ignoring messengers and acting arrogantly; the pagans similarly mistook luxury for divine favor, rejected warning and resurrection, and confined reward to wealth and punishment to poverty.
rows.anchor: فحصروا جزاء الخير في الثروة والنعمة وقصروا جزاء السوء على الخصاصة وقتر الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mistaken inference rests on denying afterlife recompense and a second life, and on imagining that present conditions last forever.
rows.anchor: وهي : إنكار الجزاء في الآخرة ، وإنكار الحياة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa branches from the universal watch-post statement: God's governance accords with His knowledge and wisdom, whereas the disbeliever reads ease as honor and hardship as humiliation.
rows.anchor: هذا شأن ربك الجاري على وفق علمه وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thinking that wealth or scarcity proves God's approval or rejection implies that divine actions lack wisdom; the Qur'an cites the same boastful inference elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وهذا التوهم يستلزم ظنهم أفعال الله تعالى جارية على غير حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches believers not to let imagination or desire distort subtle evidence: worldly conditions pass and vary in duration, refuting the prevalent pagan creed.
rows.anchor: وذكرهم بأن الأحوال الدنيوية أعراض زائلة ومتفاوتة الطول والقصر

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābighah praises the Christian Ghassānids as hoping for consequences and refusing to assume that good has no evil after it or that evil is permanent.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة في آل غسان الذين لم يكونوا مشركين وكانوا متدينين بالنصرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects both inferences because each rests on a false interpretation and deluded suspicion, as the following explanation of God's testing clarifies.
rows.anchor: مناط الردع والإبطال كلا القولين لأنهما صادران عن تأويل باطل وشبهة ضالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion singles out constrained provision because the pagans described were generally robust and healthy, dying chiefly through killing or old age among themselves or their kin.
rows.anchor: لأن غالب أحوال المشركين المتحدث عنهم صحة المزاج وقوة الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naʿʿamahu means that God placed him in a state of blessing and comfortable living.
rows.anchor: جعله في نعمة ، أي في طيب عيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaddara his provision means allotting a limited amount, a euphemism for scarcity, opposite to expanding provision.
rows.anchor: أعطاه بقدر محدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suffix in rizqihi may refer to the human as the object of allotment or to the Lord as its subject.
rows.anchor: من إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihānah is treating someone with humiliation.
rows.anchor: المعاملة بالهون وهو الذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The actions are attributed to God because blessing and allotment reach people through worldly causes and the combinations of events and circumstances He established.
rows.anchor: لأن الكرامة والنعمة انساقت للإنسان أو انساق له قدر الرزق بأسباب من جعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech is literal, expressing the person's actual belief: people boast when blessed and complain when their needs are constrained.
rows.anchor: وإنما يتكلم الانسان عن اعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting rabbī before the verb strengthens the assertion, presenting it as certain and unhesitating.
rows.anchor: أي يقول ذلك جازما به غير متردد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two conditional answers recur whenever blessing or restriction occurs; the imperfect verbs convey repeated, renewed speech.
rows.anchor: لإفادة تكرر ذلك القول وتجدده كلما حصل مضمون الشرطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes reading either ease or scarcity as God's intention to honor or humiliate; worldly status does not reveal one's standing with Him.
rows.anchor: فهو ردع عن اعتقاد ذلك فمناط الردع كلا القولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine intent is known through revelation, prophets and law, not worldly fortune; someone apparently wretched may be especially honored by God.
rows.anchor: وإنما يعرف مراد الله بالطرق التي أرشد الله إليها بواسطة رسله وشرائعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā does not deny that God truly gives blessings; it rejects the human claim that receiving them proves God's approval.
rows.anchor: أن ما ناله من النعمة علامة على رضى الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reasons for worldly treatment are hidden; the ignorant should seek truth through rational evidence and revelation rather than habitual assumptions or distorted proofs.
rows.anchor: وأن أهل الجهالة بمعزل عن إدراك سرها بأقيسة وهمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of learning place things correctly and draw sound inferences guided by revelation.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل العلم فهم يضعون الأشياء مواضعها

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read rabbī with a fatḥa on the yāʾ in both occurrences; the other readers leave it still.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو { ربي } في الموضعين بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar read qaddara with a geminated dāl, while the majority read it lightly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { فقدر عليه } بتخفيف الدال . وقرأه ابن عامر وأبو جعفر بتشديد الدال

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: Readers differ on the final yāʾ in akramanī and ahānanī: Nāfiʿ has it in connected reading only, Ibn Kathīr always, and the others listed omit it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع : { أكرمن ، وأهانن } بياء بعد النون في الوصل وبحذفها في الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted readings do not conflict with the written codex, and kallā again rejects making blessing or restricted provision signs of intended honor or humiliation.
rows.anchor: وهو مرسوم في المصحف بدون نون بعد الياءين ولا منافاة بين الرواية واسم المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke targets treating prosperity as evidence of favor, not God's actual giving of blessings; He may humiliate a disbeliever in the next life, and poverty is not imposed on every disbeliever.
rows.anchor: فمناط الردع جعل الإنعام علامة على إرادة الله إكرام المنعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal shifts from the claim that wealth is honor to the contradiction: these people hoard their surplus instead of honoring God's needy servants, exposing their boast of generosity.
rows.anchor: فنبههم الله على أنهم إن أكرمهم الله فإنهم لم يكرموا عبيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honoring an orphan means meeting the child's needs and treating him well, since he has lost a provider and may be deprived of his father's estate.
rows.anchor: سد خلته ، وحسن معاملته ، لأنه مظنة الحاجة لفقد عائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness also protects an orphan's feelings because the child senses the loss of the person who supported him.
rows.anchor: لأنه مظنة انكسار الخاطر لشعوره بفقد من يدل هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatīm is a child whose father died; the generic definite refers to orphans collectively, as in the earlier discussion in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: الصبي الذي مات أبوه وتقدم في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure even to urge feeding the poor implies, all the more, failure to feed them; their indifference means they will not even advocate for them.
rows.anchor: دلالة فحوى الخطاب ، أي لقلة الاكتراث بالمساكين لا ينفعونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām may mean food, making the poor the beneficiaries, or be the verbal noun of feeding, making them its object and the rich those to be urged.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون اسما بمعنى المطعوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miskīn means a poor person, as discussed in Sūrat al-Tawbah.
rows.anchor: الفقير وتقدم في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis to imply that they neither urge orphan guardians to honor their wards nor feed the poor from their own wealth.
rows.anchor: حصل في الآية احتباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Urging others to feed the poor can stand for feeding them oneself, since someone who advocates an act is willing to do it when able; the same usage occurs in the command to counsel truth and patience.
rows.anchor: من يحض على فعل شيء يكون راغبا في التلبس به فإذا تمكن أن يفعله فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority use second-person verbs to turn from speaking about the human to confronting the offenders; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb use third person to expose them to the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : ( لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون ) بالمثناة الفوقية

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use taḥāḍḍūn with an open ḥāʾ and an alif, a reciprocal verb whose underlying form drops one of two adjacent tāʾs.
rows.anchor: وقرأه عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف { تحاضون } بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reciprocal reading, they mutually encourage one another to refrain from urging others to feed the poor.
rows.anchor: أي تتمالؤون على ترك الحض على الإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turāth means inherited property; its original form was wirāth, with an irregular change of initial wāw to tāʾ, like several other Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: المال الموروث ، أي الذي يخلفه الرجل بعد موته لوارثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating is metaphorical for using something up without leaving any of it; Ibn ʿĀshūr had found no comparable Arabic usage and considers the metaphor Quranic in origin.
rows.anchor: مستعار للانتفاع بالشيء انتفاعا لا يبقي منه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite term stands for the inheritance of orphans, whom pre-Islamic people deprived of property left by relatives, including women and children.
rows.anchor: وتعريف التراث عوض عن المضاف إليه ، أي تراث اليتامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests wrongful appropriation: inheritance belongs to a deceased owner unable to defend it because of youth or being female.
rows.anchor: وأكله يقتضي أن يستحق ذلك المال عاجز عن الذب عن ماله لصغر أو أنوثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from threats of worldly punishment to unavoidable punishment in the next life, when compelled remembrance and regret will be useless.
rows.anchor: انتقل به من تهديدهم بعذاب الدنيا الذي في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding description of the earth's crushing and Hell is staging that builds suspense and magnifies the Day; the chief messages are the severe torment and the address to the reassured soul.
rows.anchor: فهو توطئة وتشويق لسماع ما يجيء بعده وتهويل لشأن ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakk means crushing and breaking; the earth is the inhabited globe, whose pieces will disperse as the present cosmic order collapses, through events such as earthquakes.
rows.anchor: الحطم والكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated dakkā may first function as an emphatic cognate accusative: repetition confirms literal, extraordinary crushing rather than metaphor, since this is the Quran's first mention of mountains being crushed.
rows.anchor: كان المقام مقتضيا تحقيق وقوعه حقيقة دون مجاز ولا مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second dakkā is also a verbal repetition intensifying the literal sense, since crushing the vast earth is so astonishing; the parallel in Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah is not repeated this way.
rows.anchor: منصوبا على التوكيد اللفظي لدكا الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wathāq is a verbal noun of binding, used for captives or those led to execution; Hell's people are shackled as they are dragged there.
rows.anchor: والوثاق بفتح الواو اسم مصدر أوثق وهو الربط ويجعل للأسير والمقود إلى القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wathāqahu is parsed like ʿadhābahu, an absolute object expressing comparison.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب { وثاقه } كانتصاب { عذابه } على المفعولية المطلقة لمعنى التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage ends the warnings with glad tidings for believers guided by the Quran, following the Quran's pattern of joining promise to warning to encourage good and deter evil.
rows.anchor: ختم الكلام بالبشارة للمؤمنين الذين تذكروا بالقرآن واتبعوا هديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because these verses follow the preceding passage in recitation and the codex, their original sequence likely reflects one revelation; the address is then spoken in the afterlife as an answer to the earth's crushing, with the intervening material parenthetical.
rows.anchor: فهذا قول يصدر يوم القيامة من جانب القدس من كلام الله تعالى أو من كلام الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God speaks, rabbiki replaces an implicit pronoun and expresses closeness and honor; if angels speak, it is ordinary wording, and God takes up their address by commanding the soul to enter among His servants.
rows.anchor: فإن كان من كلام الله تعالى كان قوله : { إلى ربك } إظهارا في مقام الإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God is a metaphor for dwelling in Paradise as God's honored home, like a guest's residence; the soul earned it through the divine promise to reward good works.
rows.anchor: والرجوع إلى الله مستعار للكون في نعيم الجنة التي هي دار الكرامة عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is a special homecoming to Paradise, not an unrestricted description of entry into the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهذا الرجوع خاص غير مطلق الحلول في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address may begin a new passage, prompted by the mention of punishment for the polytheist, and God may be speaking directly to the believers' reassured souls.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الآية استئنافا ابتدائيا جرى على مناسبة ذكر عذاب الإنسان المشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative to return is a promise qualified by the two following states, satisfied and approved; the return is metaphorical in this interpretation.
rows.anchor: والأمر في { ارجعي إلى ربك } مراد منه تقييده بالحالين بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person suffixes in My servants and My Paradise shift from the preceding third-person address.
rows.anchor: والإضمار في قوله : { في عبادي } وقوله : { جنتي } التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān after he donated the well of Rumah.
rows.anchor: فعن الضحاك : أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان لما تصدق ببئر رومة

rows.speaker: بريدة
rows.claim: Buraydah says the verse was revealed about Ḥamzah after his death as a martyr.
rows.anchor: وعن بريدة : أنها نزلت في حمزة حين قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported view applies the verse to Khubayb ibn ʿAdī when the Meccans crucified him; these specific occasions imply a Medinan revelation, against the agreed Meccan classification except for a report from al-Dānī.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في خبيب بن عدي لما صلبه أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse is Medinan, it is separate from the preceding passage and was placed here by instruction or revealed afterward because of thematic affinity.
rows.anchor: وهي على هذا منفصلة عما قبلها كتبت هنا بتوقيف خاص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود
rows.claim: These authorities say the words are spoken at resurrection as spirits return to bodies; on this view the passage connects to the earth being crushed, and the return is literal, with the body as the soul's Lord or owner.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابنن مسعود : أن هذا يقال عند البعث

rows.speaker: زيد بن حارثة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and Abū Ṣāliḥ say the address is given to the soul at death; Zayd specifically says the believer's soul is thereby promised Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن زيد بن حارثة وأبي صالح : يقال هذا للنفس عند الموت

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that after a man recited the verse before the Prophet and Abū Bakr praised it, the Prophet said an angel would say it to Abū Bakr at death; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقد روى الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير قال : قرأ رجل عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean the whole person, as in two cited verses, or the spirit that gives bodily life, as in another.
rows.anchor: والنفس : تطلق على الذات كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return can be understood literally or metaphorically according to the interpretations already discussed.
rows.anchor: والرجوع يحتمل الحقيقة والمجاز كما علمت من الوجوه المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāḍiyah describes a soul satisfied with its bestowed honor, indirectly expressing that it receives everything it desires.
rows.anchor: من كرامة وهو كناية عن إعطائها كل ما تطمح إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marḍiyyah is a passive participle originally meaning approved by God; deletion of the preposition makes it the grammatical subject, and the wording implies further gifts beyond what satisfied the soul.
rows.anchor: فوقع فيه الحذف والإيصال فصار نائب فاعل بدون حرف الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering among God's servants and His Paradise details the general glad tiding, repeating the joy of the promised soul.
rows.anchor: فهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال لتكرير إدخال السرور على أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants are the righteous, inferred from the honored possessive construction and its pairing with Paradise; the phrase resembles God's promise in another verse.
rows.anchor: والمراد العباد الصالحون بقرينة مقام الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among them expresses actual inclusion and, by implication, companionship with the prophets and other blessed people.
rows.anchor: فالظرفية حقيقية وتؤول إلى معنى المعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it My Paradise is an honorific attribution, as in the description of a seat of truth with a powerful king.
rows.anchor: إلى ضمير الجلالة إضافة تشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person attribution to Paradise makes the shift from God's mention in the third person aesthetically apt.
rows.anchor: وهذه الإضافة هي مما يزيد الالتفات إلى ضمير التكلم حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the command to enter, rather than using one command with both objects, emphasizes Paradise itself and secures the hearers' joy.
rows.anchor: فلم يقل : فادخلي جنتي في عبادي للاهتمام بالدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath creates suspense, and its extended wording prolongs the anticipation.
rows.anchor: ابتدئت بالقسم تشويقا لما يرد بعده وأطيلت جملة القسم زيادة في التشويق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā uqsim means 'I swear'; earlier discussion considered whether lā is an extra particle or retains negation as an indirect way to magnify the oath's object.
rows.anchor: معناه : أقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to familiar Makkah, vivid in the audience's minds from repeated sight; it fully distinguishes and honors the city.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حاضر في أذهان السامعين كأنهم يرونه لأن رؤيته متكررة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balad can mean a settled or open tract; here it denotes built-up Makkah, with a line by Ruʾbah illustrating the broader sense.
rows.anchor: جانب من متسع من أرض عامرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swearing by Makkah, although it is neither a divine attribute nor an act, signifies God's honoring and privileging it.
rows.anchor: والقسم بالبلدة مع أنها لا تدل على صفة من صفات الذات الإلاهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause 'while you are ḥill in this city' interrupts the oath's coordinated objects; its purpose depends on how ḥill is interpreted.
rows.anchor: معترضة بين المتعاطفات المقسم بها

rows.speaker: شرحبيل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sharḥabīl ibn Saʿd understands ḥill as permitted: Meccans allow themselves to harm or expel the Prophet in a sanctuary that otherwise protects its residents, game and trees.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى وقد جعلك أهل مكة حلالا بهذا البلد الذي يحرم أذى صيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading censures the Meccans for attacking God's messenger in a town where they spare even animals from harm.
rows.anchor: والمعنى التعريض بالمشركين في عدوانهم وظلمهم الرسول

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah cites an interpretation of ḥill as 'dwelling here'; Ibn al-ʿArabī mentions it without attribution, as do al-Qurṭubī and al-Bayḍāwī.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن عطية عن بعض المتأولين : أن معنى { وأنت حل بهذا البلد } أنه حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resident interpretation would make the clause circumstantial and beautifully tie the oath to the Prophet's city, but no recognized lexicon supports ḥill meaning resident; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects Khafājī's dismissal of that lexical objection.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا لم يرد في كتب اللغة : ( الصحاح ) و ( اللسان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'this city' instead of using a pronoun renews the wonder and emphasizes Makkah's eventual opening, painful for its former masters to lose.
rows.anchor: وتكرير لفظ { بهذا البلد } إظهار في مقام الإضمار لقصد تجديد التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite 'father' conveys grandeur; the context of the oath and the phrase 'and what he fathered' favor its literal sense.
rows.anchor: وقع منكرا فهو تنكير تعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father best suited to the city's context is Abraham, who established Makkah for his son Ishmael and Hagar.
rows.anchor: والذي يناسب القسم بهذا البلد أن يكون المراد ب { والد } إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is also the father of Makkah's original inhabitants and the Prophet's ancestor.
rows.anchor: وإبراهيم والد سكان ذلك البلد الأصليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about whether anyone saw him elaborates on his claim to have spent much wealth: he assumes everyone will believe a boast that some people can recognize as false.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { يقول أهلكت مالا } لأن قوله

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse says a person's character becomes known even if he thinks it is hidden from people, supporting the claim that the boaster's lie is observable.
rows.anchor:
قال زهير :
ومهما تكن عند امرىء من خليقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative rebukes and denies his assumption, indirectly asserting God's knowledge of his inner motives and exposing his false boast of generosity.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار وتوبيخ وهو كناية عن علم الله تعالى بدخيلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read lubadan with a short u and open bāʾ as the plural of a clump of wool or hair matted together.
rows.anchor: و { لبدا } بضم اللام وفتح الموحدة في قراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads lubaddan with a geminated bāʾ, parsing it either as a plural of lābid, 'gathered together,' or as a noun on the faʿal pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر { لبدا } بضم اللام وتشديد الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verses explain the rebuke: the creator of human perception and speech must know and be able to judge people's acts.
rows.anchor: فكيف يكون مفيض العلم على الناس غير قادر وغير عالم بأحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question may seek assent or reject the boast; eyes are singled out as the most useful senses and directly answer his claim that nobody saw him.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار على العينين لأنهما أنفع المشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both lips and tongue are named because speech requires their cooperation; the Quran pictures the creation of the speech apparatus more fully than ordinary Arab idiom does.
rows.anchor: ومن دقائق القرآن أنه لم يقتصر على اللسان ولا على الشفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The progression completes the foundations of learning: senses acquire knowledge, speech communicates it, and guidance helps distinguish and test good and evil.
rows.anchor: فاستكمل الكلام أصول التعلم والتعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lips cover the mouth and teeth, help draw in water, and shape letter sounds through opening and closing; their speech function is the point here.
rows.anchor: ومن انفتاحهما وانغلاقهما تتكيف أصوات الحروف التي بها النطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word shafah may derive from shafw with omitted wāw and a compensating hāʾ, or from an original hāʾ; Ibn ʿĀshūr favors original hāʾ treated like feminine hāʾ for ease, reflected in the dual shafatayn.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الأصل شفه بهاء أصلية ثم عوملت الهاء معاملة هاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hidāyah is showing the route to a destination; najd is elevated terrain short of a mountain, and the two routes may be an ascent or a low hollow.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على الطريق المبلغة إلى المكان المقصود السير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is metaphorical for innate discernment of benefit and harm, grounding human society, knowledge and the Islamic path to salvation.
rows.anchor: وقد استعيرت الهداية هنا للإلهام الذي جعله الله في الإنسان يدرك به الضار والنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two high paths represent good and evil: good is hard to follow, while evil has hard consequences, explaining the next verse's image of an uphill pass.
rows.anchor: واستعير النجدان للخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymanah means either the right-hand side, from being on one's right, or blessedness; the roots are related, and right-hand orientation was associated with practical benefit and prosperity.
rows.anchor: فهي مفعلة للمكان مأخوذة من فعل يمنه ( فعلا ماضيا ) إذا كان على يمينه

rows.speaker: المرقش
rows.claim: Al-Muraqqish's verse argues that ill-omened signs can be like auspicious ones and auspicious signs like ill-omened ones, exposing the convention as reversible.
rows.anchor:
قال المرقش يفند ذلك :
فإذا الأشائم كالأيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yemen lay to the right and was famed as prosperous Arabia Felix, while al-Shām was north and called from shāʾm; the Prophet's prayer for both regions rejects associating them with omens.
rows.anchor: وقد أبطل الإسلام ذلك بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم بارك لنا في شأمنا وفي يمننا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left hand's name yasar likewise counters any superstition that it is unlucky; Arabs honored right-side seating at gatherings and demeaned the opposite side.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت جهة اليمين جهة مكرمة تعارفوا الجلوس على اليمين في المجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam abolished preferred seating, so people sit wherever they reach the gathering.
rows.anchor: وقد أبطله الإسلام فكان الناس يجلسون حين انتهى بهم المجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's people are called أصحاب الميمنة and أصحاب اليمين, while Hell's people are أصحاب المشأمة and أصحاب الشمال; these names mark honor or its opposite.
rows.anchor: وسمي أهل الجنة { أصحاب الميمنة } و { أصحاب اليمين } ( الواقعة : 27 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣḥāb al-mashʾamah means the debased; the name is metaphorical from Arab social custom, not a literal direction, which would require a spatial referent.
rows.anchor: أي هم محقرون . وذلك كناية مبنية على عرف العرب يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause completes the earlier censure by first praising and promising the righteous, then returning to warn the offenders; the arrangement echoes its opening and contrasts right and left.
rows.anchor: محسن رد العجز على الصدر ، ومحسن الطباق بين الميمنة والمشأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left-side group represents humiliation and anger, so the following verse says that a sealed fire awaits them.
rows.anchor: أتبع بقوله : { عليهم نار مؤصدة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separator pronoun in 'they are the left-side people' strengthens the assertion but does not itself restrict the class; contrast with the prior sentence supplies exclusivity.
rows.anchor: وضمير الفصل في قوله : { هم أصحاب المشأمة } لتقوية الحكم وليس للقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʾṣadah is passive from awṣada, 'shut a door'; a hamzated form is another dialect, possibly Qurashī, and it may also be linked to waṣīdah, a mountain-stone shelter for camels.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أأصد بالهمز وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read mūṣadah with wāw; Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, Yaʿqūb and Khalaf read it with a hamzah, from the alternate verb and with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: فقرأ الجمهور : { موصدة } بواو ساكنة بعد الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the shut fire may replace the preceding statement by apposition or explain it as an answer to an implied question.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { هم أصحاب المشأمة } أو استئناف بياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting 'upon them' emphasizes the enclosure and hastens the threat; attributing closure to the fire is a figurative attribution to Hell, the place where it burns.
rows.anchor: وقدم على عامله للاهتمام بتعلق الغلق عليهم تعجيلا للترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about inspiration is coordinated with the soul's fashioning, and its fa signals that inspiration arises from that fashioning; the pronoun may refer to the act of straightening.
rows.anchor: وعطف بالفاء لأن الإلهام ناشىء عن التسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā may be relative and refer to God's act: building the sky, spreading the earth and straightening the soul.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { ما } موصولة صادقة على فعل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Soul's physical and mental capacities are adjusted from completion of embryonic formation and early childhood, then develop in quality until inspiration occurs.
rows.anchor: فالتسوية حاصلة من وقت تمام خلقة الجنين من أول أطوار الصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilhām is a verbal noun of alhama; the simple verb is obsolete, the noun is rare, and lexicographers cited no Arabic poetic evidence for it.
rows.anchor: مصدر ألهم ، وهو فعل متعد بالهمزة ولكن المجرد منه ممات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its specialized sense, ilhām is knowledge arriving in the soul without teaching, experience or thought, whether innate and necessary or reached through evidence and reasoning.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الإلهام إطلاقا خاصا على حدوث علم في النفس بدون تعليم ولا تجربة ولا تفكير

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ilhām as placing something in the heart and limits it to what comes from God or the higher angelic realm.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الإلهام : إيقاع الشيء في الروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran may have coined this precise psychological term or revived it; its root conveys gulping, while Sufis use it technically for unsupported knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فهذا اللفظ إن لم يكن من مبتكرات القرآن يكن مما أحياه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the soul's constitution produces primary and necessary cognition, instincts such as a baby's first search for the breast or avoidance of harm, and eventually the beginnings of rational acquisition.
rows.anchor: ابتداء من الانسياق الجبلي نحو الأمور النافعة كطلب الرضيع الثدي أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innate discernment makes the divinely revealed distinction between transgression and piety intelligible; without minds, people could not grasp commands, punishment or reward.
rows.anchor: فلولا العقول لما تيسر إفهام الإنسان الفجور والتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fujūr precedes taqwā because the surah addresses polytheists, whose deeds were mostly transgression, while Muslims were then few.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الفجور على التقوى مراعى فيه أحوال المخاطبين بهذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine form alhamahā treats the verbal noun taswiyah as nonfeminine or follows the masculine form of mā if it is relative.
rows.anchor: ومجيء فعل : ( ألهمها ) بصيغة الإسناد إلى ضمير مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The success-and-failure statement may answer the oath, like the answer in Sūrat al-Layl, or interrupt it to explain that the soul succeeds by choosing its divinely indicated piety.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الجملة جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This contrast prepares the lesson of Thamūd: their punishment followed from corrupting their souls through arrogance.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة توطئة لجملة : كذبت ثمود بطغواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human who purifies the soul and that soul are the same being, presented as two because of choice and action; tazkiyah means increasing goodness.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان والنفس شيء واحد ، ونزلا منزلة شيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dassāhā means preventing the soul from good; its root is hiding something beneath another, with consonant substitution for ease as in other Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: حال بينها وبين فعل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If success and failure answer the oath, Thamūd's denial is evidence for the failure of those who corrupt their souls.
rows.anchor: في موقع الدليل لمضمون جملة { وقد خاب من دساها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success is attaining one's aim and failure is being deprived of it; lasting good is true success, while transient gain that turns into decline is failure, ultimately in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: النجاح بحصول المطلوب ، والخيبة ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage repeatedly uses antithesis: sun and moon, day and night, disclosure and concealment, heaven and earth, building and spreading, transgression and piety, success and failure, purification and corruption.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات محسن الطباق غير مرة فقد ذكرت أشياء متقابلة متضادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the success statement is parenthetical, the story's consequence of Thamūd's destruction answers the oath; its lām is omitted to shorten an already long oath, as in Sūrat al-Burūj.
rows.anchor: ولام الجواب محذوف تخفيفا لاستطالة القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath indirectly threatens the arrogant Quraysh, who resemble Thamūd in knowingly rejecting the Messenger; God swears they will suffer a like punishment.
rows.anchor: التعريض بتهديد المشركين الذين كذبوا الرسول طغيانا هم يعلمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans had experienced the sword's punishment at the hands of enemies after persecuting and expelling the Prophet, a particularly bitter chastisement.
rows.anchor: ولقد أصاب المشركين عذاب السيف بأيدي الذين عادوهم وآذوهم وأخرجوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of 'denied' is omitted but supplied from the next clause: Thamūd denied their Messenger.
rows.anchor: فمفعول { كذبت } محذوف لدلالة قوله بعده : { فقال لهم رسول الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in biṭaghwā expresses cause: extreme arrogance caused them to deny the Messenger; this parallels Quraysh's pride at following someone they thought socially inferior.
rows.anchor: وباء { بطغواها } للسببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time of the worst arrogance was when they chose their most wicked man to hamstring the she-camel, the climax of their defiance.
rows.anchor: لأن وقت انبعاث أشقاها لعقر الناقة هو الوقت الذي بدت فيه شدة طغواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inbaʿatha is the middle form of baʿatha: they sent the man, and he volunteered for the deed.
rows.anchor: مطاوع بعث ، فالمعنى : إذ بعثوا أشقاهم فانبعث وانتدب لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase is brought forward because the worst man's rising is a particular instance of their arrogance and closely explains its cause; the wording still implies this happened after Salih's warning.
rows.anchor: وقدم ذكر هذا الظرف عن موقعه بعد قوله : { فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله }

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators identify the most wretched man as Qidār ibn Sālif; he exceeded the others in directly committing the crime, although they incited him.
rows.anchor: وعني به رجل منهم سماه المفسرون قدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first fa sequences the denial and Salih's challenge: he showed the she-camel as a sign and warned them not to harm it or deprive it of its turn to drink.
rows.anchor: فتحداهم بآية الناقة وحذرهم من التعرض لها بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later 'they denied him' means they rejected the warning and its threatened punishment; thus the she-camel sign followed an earlier rejection, as in the account in Sūrat Hūd.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن آية الناقة أرسلت لهم بعد أن كذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fa merely introduces details after a general statement, as in other Quranic examples; Thamūd denied through arrogance when their most wicked man rose, with the warning and hamstringing then elaborating the episode.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural pronouns are used because Thamūd are a people collectively, although the earlier reference treats Thamūd grammatically as a tribe name.
rows.anchor: وأعيدت عليهم ضمائر الجمع باعتبار أنهم جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāqata Allāh is accusative as a warning: beware God's she-camel means do not harm her, with the command attached to the creature but intended for people's conduct.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { ناقة الله } على التحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive honors the she-camel as God's sign confirming Salih's mission and as a miraculous creature.
rows.anchor: وإضافة { ناقة } إلى اسم الجلالة لأنها آية جعلها الله على صدق رسالة صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siqyāhā is a verbal noun following the warning: beware taking her allotted water, with either an omitted noun such as the water source or a source term used for the water itself.
rows.anchor: والسقيا : اسم مصدر سقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended prohibition is inferred from context: they must not water their camels on her day, since the word siqyā points to her assigned turn.
rows.anchor: فإن مادة سقيا تؤذن بأن المراد التحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial following the warning is a second denial: they rejected the threat implied by the prohibition, as stated explicitly in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: والتكذيب المعقب به تحذيره إياهم بقوله : { ناقة الله } ، تكذيب ثانن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAqr is wounding a camel's forelegs so pain makes it kneel for slaughter at the breast; because the acts are connected, the word conventionally implies slaughter.
rows.anchor: جرح البعير في يديه ليبرك على الأرض من الألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads damdama as God's angry shout, the sound of the lightning and quake that destroyed them; its attribution to God is figurative because He creates the sound and its qualities.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهذه الدمدمة صوت الصاعقة والرجفة التي أهلكوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators instead interpret damdama as covering them with the earth, from the verb damm for covering a grave; reduplication intensifies the meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين : دمدم عليهم أطبق عليهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn ʿĀshūr's reading, sawāhā means the punishment struck them evenly; its feminine pronoun refers to the dundering/punishment understood from damdama.
rows.anchor: فاستووا في إصابتها لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who take damdama as burying them understand sawāhā to mean the earth became level over them, hiding their bodies and dwellings; its pronoun then refers to the implicit earth.
rows.anchor: جعل الأرض مستوية عليهم لا تظهر فيها أجسادهم ولا بلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase fa-sawwāhā forms complete paronomasia with wa-mā sawwāhā earlier in the same surah.
rows.anchor: وبين { فسواها } هنا وقوله : { وما سواها } ( الشمس : 7 ) قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUqbā is the consequence or reward after an act; conventionally, the defeated fear revenge, but God is the victor whom no defeated people can retaliate against, showing delayed punishment is respite rather than weakness.
rows.anchor: أخبر الله أنه الغالب الذي لا يقدر مغلوبه على أخذ الثأر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may instead portray their eradication as leaving no survivor to seek vengeance, a figure for total destruction.
rows.anchor: تمثيلا لحالهم في الاستئصال بحال من لم يترك من يثأر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar read fa-lā yakhāfu with fa, deriving it from the destruction and concluding that God need not fear their retaliation; this reading appears in the Medina and Syria codices.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر { فلا يخاف عقباها } بفاء العطف تفريعا على { فدمدم عليهم ربهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest of the ten readers use wāw, as either coordination or circumstantial conjunction, matching the Meccan, Basran and Kufan codices.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون من العشرة : { ولا يخاف عقباها } بواو العطف أو الحال

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم وابن وهب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim and Ibn Wahb say Mālik showed them his grandfather's codex, reportedly copied during ʿUthmān's codex project, reading wa-lā yakhāfu with wāw.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم وابن وهب : أخرج لنا مالك مصحفا لجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This report implies some Medinan codices had wāw, although local readers rejected that reading because it conflicted with their transmitted recitation.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن بعض مصاحف المدينة بالواو ولكنهم لم يقرأوا بذلك لمخالفته روايتهم
